1.title: Q2 global semiconductor revenue hits a record US$425 billion, up 31.4% QoQ; memory accounts for over half
1.summary: According to an Omdia report, global semiconductor revenue reached US$425 billion in Q2 2026, up 31.4% quarter-on-quarter — the strongest quarter since tracking began in Q1 2002. First-half revenue totaled US$752 billion, and Q3 is forecast to exceed US$500 billion. Memory ICs made up more than half of total revenue, with DRAM, NAND and NOR each posting record quarterly growth for the second straight quarter. Microprocessor (MPU) revenue rose 16% QoQ, far above the typical seasonal growth of about 1%. The last four quarters, dating back to Q3 2025, have all delivered double-digit sequential growth.
1.metric: Q2 revenue US$425B (QoQ +31.4%); 1H26 total US$752B; Q3 forecast >US$500B; MPU +16% QoQ (seasonal norm ~1%); four straight quarters of double-digit QoQ growth
1.impact: With memory taking more than half, a sizable part of this revenue surge comes from pricing rather than foundry wafer volume. But the 16% jump in MPUs matches this period's analysis of Meta Muse driving CPU demand, showing AI demand is spilling over from GPUs to CPUs and other logic chips — and that lands directly on the leading-edge capacity of TSMC and Intel Foundry.
1.conf: Confirmed (research firm data; Q3 is a forecast)

2.entity: Ministry of Economic Affairs / Taiwan export orders
2.title: August export orders top US$100 billion for the first time at US$102.96 billion, up 71.4% YoY; full year could reach US$1.1 trillion
2.summary: Taiwan's Ministry of Economic Affairs (MOEA) reported August export orders of US$102.96 billion, the first month ever above US$100 billion, up 71.4% year-on-year and the 19th consecutive month of growth. Orders for information and communication products reached US$34.21 billion (+100.5% YoY), and electronic products US$45.75 billion (+83.9% YoY). The MOEA expects September orders of US$106.0–109.1 billion (+50.7% to 55.1% YoY), putting the full year on track for about US$1.1 trillion.
2.metric: Aug export orders US$102.96B (YoY +71.4%); ICT US$34.21B (YoY +100.5%); electronics US$45.75B (YoY +83.9%); Sep forecast US$106.0–109.1B; full year up to ~US$1.1T
2.impact: Electronics orders (including foundry and ICs) grew more than 80% YoY — the data behind the central bank's decision last week to raise its 2026 GDP growth forecast to 11.48%. With September still expected to grow over 50% YoY, TSMC's September revenue (due around Oct 10) is very likely to stay at elevated levels.
2.conf: Confirmed (official statistics; September and full-year figures are MOEA forecasts)

3.title: TSMC reportedly pulls A14 trial production forward to 2027Q1; N3, N2/A16 and A14 to ramp simultaneously in 2027
3.summary: Commercial Times, citing IC design companies, reported that TSMC's A14 may begin trial production in 2027Q1 at Fab 20 in Baoshan, Hsinchu — earlier than originally planned. At Fab 25 in the Central Taiwan Science Park, the main A14 volume production site, floor construction for P1 is under way and could be finished before April 2027, with trial production as early as the start of Q3; P2–P4 are also being rushed. In 2027, TSMC will face the rare situation of expanding or trialing three advanced nodes at once — N3, N2/A16 and A14. Analysts estimate 3nm monthly capacity in the Southern Taiwan Science Park at about 170,000–180,000 wafers in Q4 this year, likely topping 200,000 next year; 2nm monthly capacity should reach 90,000–100,000 wafers by year-end and 130,000–140,000 in 2027. At its July earnings call, TSMC disclosed that A14 test vehicles had reached close to 90% of device performance targets, with 256Mb SRAM yield also near 90%. A13 and A12 are planned for volume production in 2029; A13 is design-rule backward-compatible with A14, and A12 introduces backside power delivery. TrendForce puts combined Fab 20 and Fab 25 capacity at about 60,000–70,000 wafers per month, and Intel CEO Lip-Bu Tan expects 14A risk production to also fall in 2027Q1.
3.metric: A14 trial production: Fab 20 in 2027Q1, Fab 25 as early as the start of 2027Q3; Fab 25 P1 completed before Apr 2027; 3nm capacity 170–180k wafers/month → over 200k in 2027; 2nm capacity 90–100k wafers/month → 130–140k in 2027; A14 device performance and 256Mb SRAM yield both near 90%; A13/A12 volume production in 2029
3.impact: Read alongside last week's news — the Longtan A14 campus clearing its first National Development Council review, and C.C. Wei saying capacity forecasts have 'become larger' — TSMC's angstrom-era timeline is being pulled forward across the board. With A14 trial production and Intel 14A risk production both landing in 2027Q1, Intel has less room to win external customers by 'matching the schedule', while TSMC must shoulder equipment and staffing needs for three nodes at once.
3.conf: Unconfirmed (the earlier trial production comes from IC designers and has not been announced by TSMC; capacity figures are analyst estimates)

4.title: Huawei's Ascend 960 arrives early but won't expand overseas; Eric Xu: SMIC's 7nm/6nm capacity is insufficient
4.summary: Huawei rotating chairman Eric Xu said demand for the new Ascend 900-series AI chips 'cannot even be met domestically', so Huawei has no plan for a broad international rollout and will supply only limited volumes to a few countries with especially strong demand. Reports point to SMIC's inability to raise 7nm and 6nm capacity as the core bottleneck, with tight HBM supply as another constraint. On the roadmap, the Ascend 960DT (training; FP8 2 PFLOPS, FP4 4 PFLOPS, 288GB HBM) has been pulled forward to 2027Q1, the 960PR (inference; FP4 8 PFLOPS, 192GB) follows in 2027Q3, and the 970 and 980 are planned for 2028 and 2029. An Atlas supercluster can link up to 15,488 Ascend 960 chips for a peak of 30 EFLOPS (FP8) / 120 EFLOPS (FP4), but overall power consumption is high and performance per watt trails Nvidia. Huawei will instead give overseas academic and research institutions access through cloud services.
4.metric: Ascend 960DT 2027Q1, 960PR 2027Q3, 970 in 2028, 980 in 2029; cluster up to 15,488 chips, 30 EFLOPS (FP8) / 120 EFLOPS (FP4); bottlenecks: SMIC 7/6nm capacity, HBM
4.impact: This is the period's most important China foundry story: Huawei's leadership has confirmed the demand side itself, and the constraint lies entirely in SMIC's advanced-node capacity. With EUV under export controls, SMIC's N+2/N+3 expansion depends on DUV multi-patterning yields and access to tools — the other side of the same problem as last week's Chinese Academy of Sciences research on extending DUV with GAA structures. It also explains why SMIC's revenue growth (19.4% YoY in this period's A-share results) lags far behind Hua Hong and Nexchip: the structural cause is not weak demand.
4.conf: Confirmed (public remarks by Huawei executives; SMIC capacity figures not disclosed)

5.title: Alibaba unveils Zhenwu V900 AI chip: volume production in 2027Q1, three times the performance of its predecessor
5.summary: Alibaba unveiled its next-generation Zhenwu V900 AI chip, featuring 216GB of memory, 1,200GB/s chip-to-chip bandwidth and support for FP8 and FP4 compute, delivering three times the performance of the previous M890. Volume production is expected in 2027Q1; its ICN Switch can connect up to 500,000 V900s to train models with 5–10 trillion parameters. Alibaba also plans the Zhenwu J900 and Yitian 720/730 server CPUs for 2027Q3, with the Yitian 730 being its first CPU with a fully in-house microarchitecture. Alibaba has pledged more than US$53 billion over three years for AI infrastructure, targeting over 20GW of global data-center capacity by 2032. The report did not disclose the foundry or process node.
5.metric: V900: 216GB memory, 1,200GB/s, 3× the M890, volume production 2027Q1; cluster limit 500,000 chips; Yitian 720/730 in 2027Q3; AI infrastructure >US$53B over three years
5.impact: Read together with the Huawei and DeepSeek items, China's 2027 wave of AI chip launches is already scheduled — but all of them need domestic advanced-node capacity. If SMIC makes the V900, it will compete directly with Ascend for scarce 7/6nm capacity; the undisclosed foundry itself reflects how sensitive the issue is under export controls.
5.conf: Confirmed (company launch; foundry and process not disclosed)

6.title: Meta Muse reveals agentic AI's appetite for CPUs: 100 million users would need an estimated 1.58 million CPUs
6.summary: Meta's AI agent Muse topped the App Store download chart. Based on its architecture of 'one always-on cloud virtual machine per user', market analysts estimate that 100 million users would ideally require about 1.58 million AMD Ryzen-class CPUs, 800PB of memory and 10,000PB of SSD storage (2 vCPUs, 8GB of memory and 100GB of storage per user). TrendForce notes that agentic AI needs a higher CPU-to-GPU ratio, which should benefit Intel, AMD and Arm; however, the industry also points out that real deployments can sharply cut resource use through idle hibernation, on-demand startup and core sharing.
6.metric: 100M users ≈ 1.58M CPUs, 800PB memory, 10,000PB SSD; 2 vCPU / 8GB / 100GB per user
6.impact: Agentic AI extends compute demand from GPUs to general-purpose CPUs, which for foundries means more diversified sources of advanced-node demand: AMD (TSMC N3/N2), Arm-camp custom CPUs (TSMC) and Intel (its own 18A) all get a share. It is the same trend as this period's Alibaba Yitian CPUs and Omdia's 16% QoQ MPU growth.
6.conf: Unconfirmed (external analyst estimate; actual deployments may use far fewer resources)

7.title: Episil-Precision targets 35%+ revenue growth this year; 8-inch silicon epitaxy fully loaded, some prices raised from Q3
7.summary: Epitaxial wafer maker Episil-Precision expects full-year revenue to grow more than 35% this year, with AI-related revenue rising to 30% of the total and over 40% in 2027. Q2 revenue was about NT$1.309 billion (+23.6% QoQ), and August consolidated revenue was about NT$507 million (+57.79% YoY). Its 8-inch silicon epitaxy capacity remains fully loaded, with PMIC and MOSFET output up about 50% YoY. In compound semiconductors, GaN has turned profitable with 6-inch capacity fully loaded, while SiC losses have narrowed sharply. Its germanium-silicon photodetectors have passed international customer qualification and entered volume production; silicon photonics revenue could grow 2.5× in the second half, reaching 3%–5% of monthly revenue by year-end. The company has raised prices on some products since Q3 to reflect higher raw-material and operating costs; first-half capex was about NT$900 million, with benefits mainly showing in 2027–2028.
7.metric: 2026 revenue YoY >35%; AI revenue share 30% → >40% in 2027; Q2 revenue ~NT$1.309B (QoQ +23.6%); Aug revenue ~NT$507M (YoY +57.79%); PMIC/MOSFET output YoY ~+50%; 1H26 capex ~NT$900M
7.impact: Episil-Precision is an upstream epitaxy supplier for mature-node power devices. Its fully loaded 8-inch lines, 50% higher PMIC/MOSFET output and new price hikes match exactly what drove last week's 'noticeable price increases' at UMC and PSMC (AI peripheral components) — confirming from upstream that this mature-node cycle reflects real demand rather than inventory restocking.
7.conf: Confirmed (company briefing; full-year growth and revenue mix are company forecasts)

8.title: Foreign broker sets GUC target price at NT$12,000, sees 5× N3/N5 allocation in 2027; Daiwa gives WinWay NT$10,000
8.summary: Aletheia Capital initiated coverage of GUC with a Buy rating and a NT$12,000 target price, arguing that agentic AI is pushing cloud service providers and AI labs to accelerate in-house ASICs, making GUC — with its advanced-packaging IP, turnkey services and close ties to TSMC's DTP division — a key beneficiary. It forecasts GUC's N3/N5 wafer allocation will rise fivefold in 2027, with revenue doubling in 2026 and then growing fourfold in 2027; 2026 EPS of NT$52.75 and 2027 EPS of NT$123.46; and a 35%–40% CAGR for the global AI ASIC market over 2025–2028. The same day Daiwa reiterated its Buy on WinWay with a NT$10,000 target, raising its Q3 revenue estimate by 9.3% to NT$5.012 billion because capacity at the new Renwu, Kaohsiung plant came online faster than expected; it forecasts 2026 revenue of NT$16.57 billion (+111% YoY) and NT$30.37 billion in 2027. GUC shares hit limit-up on 9/22.
8.metric: GUC: target NT$12,000, 2027 N3/N5 allocation ×5, 2026 EPS NT$52.75, 2027 EPS NT$123.46; AI ASIC CAGR 35–40%; WinWay: target NT$10,000, Q3 revenue estimate NT$5.012B, 2026 revenue NT$16.57B (YoY +111%)
8.impact: A multiplied allocation for ASIC design services ultimately means TSMC N3/N5 wafer orders, while capacity expansion at test-interface makers is a leading indicator of advanced-node shipments. Both being upgraded on the same day shows the market widening the circle of foundry-growth beneficiaries to design services and the test supply chain.
8.conf: Confirmed (broker reports; revenue and EPS are broker estimates, not company guidance)

9.title: Korea's HBM-related exports to Malaysia jump 5.7× in a year as AI packaging demand spills into Southeast Asia
9.summary: Korea's HBM-related exports to Malaysia grew 5.7-fold in one year, with export weight rising from 1.4 to 3.8 tonnes; in August, exports of multi-chip integrated circuits (HS 8542.32.3000) reached US$1.62 billion. Malaysia accounts for about 13% of global semiconductor assembly and test, and aims for a 7% share of global advanced packaging by 2035. ASE opened its fifth plant in Penang last year, TF-AMD plans to add bumping and advanced-packaging services by end-2026, and Intel's Project Pelican is a US$7 billion investment. The report argues that with Taiwan's advanced-packaging capacity tight and TSMC's CoWoS orders full, Malaysia can take on more back-end work — but not replace TSMC.
9.metric: HBM-related exports ×5.7 (one year); weight 1.4 → 3.8 tonnes; Aug multi-chip IC exports US$1.62B; Malaysia ~13% of global OSAT, 7% advanced-packaging target by 2035; Intel Pelican US$7B
9.impact: Read with last week's TSMC Kaohsiung Mini-Loop and CoWoS overflow to Amkor: front-end work remains concentrated in Taiwan, but testing after HBM stacking and some back-end steps are dispersing to Malaysia, providing a capacity buffer for the ASE, Intel and AMD packaging-and-test chains.
9.conf: Confirmed (customs data; the industry interpretation is media analysis)

10.title: Lumentum, Qualcomm and Corning demo a 1060nm VCSEL optical die-to-die interconnect; US optical stocks rally
10.summary: Lumentum announced a collaboration with Qualcomm and Corning to demonstrate, at ECOC 2026, a high-density die-to-die (D2D) optical interconnect for AI data-center scale-up. Combining Qualcomm's D2D interface IP, Lumentum's 1060nm VCSEL optical platform (about 10 Tb/s) and Corning's multimode fiber connectors, it can extend D2D links to tens of meters while keeping latency and power low, targeting future CPO and NPO applications. The news lifted US optical-communication stocks: Lumentum rose 2.53%, Corning 5.89%, and InP substrate maker AXT jumped 14.14% on its inclusion in the S&P SmallCap 600 index.
10.impact: VCSELs moving from short-reach data-center optical modules to chip-to-chip interconnect expands the addressable market for compound-semiconductor foundries (the VCSEL and InP processes at WIN Semiconductors and Advanced Wireless Semiconductor). It also complements last week's reports of silicon photonics spreading into lidar and biomedicine — optical interconnect is advancing on silicon and compound platforms at the same time.
10.conf: Confirmed (company announcement; share prices are US closes on 9/21, for reference only)

11.title: SOX jumps 4.29% to a record high; Taiwan index futures gain 728 points in the night session, breaking 48,000
11.summary: On 9/21 the Philadelphia Semiconductor Index (SOX) surged 4.29% to an all-time high, driven mainly by an ~10% jump in AMD and reports of major progress in US-China trade talks during the Trump-Xi meeting; the US 10-year Treasury yield eased to 4.96%, reducing valuation pressure on tech stocks. TSMC's ADR rose 1.02% to US$434.67. Taiwan index futures jumped 728 points in the night session, breaking above 48,000. In the previous Taiwan session, the three major institutional investors were net buyers of NT$4.78 billion, with money concentrated in ASIC, advanced packaging, ABF substrate and optoelectronics names.
11.metric: SOX +4.29% (record); AMD ~+10%; TSMC ADR US$434.67 (+1.02%); US 10-yr yield 4.96%; TAIEX futures night session +728 pts, above 48K; institutional net buying NT$4.78B
11.impact: Progress in US-China talks is the only positive policy signal this period, but the reports gave no specifics, so it is impossible to tell whether semiconductor export controls will ease. AMD's big gain echoes the thesis that agentic AI is driving CPU demand.
11.conf: Confirmed (market data; details of the US-China progress not disclosed; closing prices for reference only)

12.title: TAIEX hits an intraday record of 48,601 but fades, closing up just 81 points at 47,800; TSMC turns lower to close at NT$2,460
12.summary: On 9/22 the TAIEX rallied more than 800 points intraday to a record 48,601, but profit-taking set in and it closed up just 81.33 points at 47,800.17 — the day's low — on turnover of about NT$1.02 trillion. TSMC opened higher at NT$2,510, reclaiming NT$2,500, but turned negative around midday and closed at NT$2,460, down NT$20 (-0.81%); Commercial Times estimated TSMC's pullback from its high cost the index about 360 points. MediaTek rose more than 3%, hitting a record NT$5,480 intraday, as money rotated into IC design and substrates: Unimicron, Kinsus and Nan Ya PCB rose, Xintec became the first Taiwan stock priced above NT$20,000, and GUC hit limit-up.
12.metric: TAIEX 47,800.17 (+81.33), intraday high 48,601, turnover ~NT$1.02T; TSMC NT$2,460 (-20, -0.81%), intraday high NT$2,510; MediaTek intraday high NT$5,480
12.impact: Cross-check: 9/21 close 47,718.84 + 81.33 = 47,800.17; TSMC 2,480 − 20 = 2,460 — both consistent. TSMC pulled back after a strong run while money rotated into ASIC design services and substrates, in line with GUC and WinWay getting higher target prices the same day — the market is digesting 'foundry beneficiaries beyond TSMC'.
12.conf: Confirmed (closing prices for reference only, not current prices)

13.title: Intel EMIB substrate yield reportedly rises to ~45%; suppliers target 60% by 2027Q1
13.summary: Reports say Intel's EMIB substrate yield rose to about 45% in the latest quarter (from about 30% in Q2 2026), with targets of 50% in Q4 2026 and 60% in Q1 2027. The main suppliers are Japan's Ibiden and Shinko Electric and Taiwan's Unimicron, with Samsung Electro-Mechanics and LG Innotek also reportedly keen to enter. On the customer side, Google is expected to adopt EMIB-T in 2027, AWS is testing it, and MediaTek has adopted a dual-packaging strategy. EMIB embeds silicon bridges directly in the substrate rather than using an interposer; the thermal-expansion mismatch between ABF and silicon, and air bubbles trapped when NCF material is bonded, are the main yield obstacles. Intel's CEO said the company even has to make prepayments to secure supplier commitment.
13.metric: EMIB substrate yield: ~30% in 2Q26 → ~45% → 50% target in 4Q26 → 60% target in 1Q27; suppliers Ibiden, Shinko, Unimicron; Google to adopt EMIB-T in 2027
13.impact: EMIB-T is Intel Foundry's most practical entry point for winning external AI customers, but a 45% substrate yield shows it is unlikely to shake CoWoS-L in the near term (TrendForce last week expected CoWoS-L to stay dominant through 2028). For Unimicron, it is a second source of high-end substrate demand beyond CoWoS.
13.conf: Unconfirmed (supply-chain reports; Intel has not disclosed yield figures)

14.entity: BOE / Samsung Electro-Mechanics / SKC / LG Innotek / Intel
14.title: Glass substrate race speeds up: BOE joins, Korean makers aim for 2027–2028 mass production, Intel reveals a new glass substrate patent
14.summary: BOE has produced 24-layer glass substrates larger than 100×100mm and completed internal reliability tests, aiming to finalize mass production investment needs by mid-2027 and reach full mass production in 2028; at IPC 2026 it showed a TGV substrate with a 15:1 aspect ratio (up from 10:1). Reports say Nvidia has asked substrate makers to speed up development, so adoption may come before 2028. Among Korean players, Samsung Electro-Mechanics and Dongwoo Fine-Chem (a Sumitomo Chemical subsidiary) formed the joint venture GlaSSEM, targeting mass production in 2027; SKC is injecting another KRW 92.1 billion into its US subsidiary Absolics (KRW 373.1 billion in total); and LG Innotek targets mass production in 2028. CSOT has also set up a packaging validation team and will release samples by year-end. Separately, on 9/22 Intel published a Micro LED packaging patent that embeds dies in a glass substrate with power delivered through TGVs; Intel plans to mass-produce and ship glass substrates from its US$3.3 billion plant in India in 2028–2030.
14.metric: BOE: 24 layers, >100×100mm, TGV aspect ratio 15:1, mass production 2028; SKC adds KRW 92.1B to Absolics (KRW 373.1B cumulative); Samsung Electro-Mechanics' GlaSSEM mass production 2027; LG Innotek 2028; Intel India plant US$3.3B, mass production 2028–2030
14.impact: A direct comparison with last week's report that TSMC's CoPoS is in talks for an AUO site (square glass substrates + TGV): panel makers (AUO, BOE, CSOT) leveraging their glass-processing experience to enter advanced packaging has become a cross-border trend. If Nvidia's push pulls glass substrate mass production forward, it will set the competitive pace between TSMC CoPoS and Intel's glass packaging.
14.conf: Confirmed (company progress from public demos and investment announcements; Nvidia's request to accelerate is a media report)

15.title: China A-share chipmakers' 1H net profit up 607%: CXMT tops revenue and profit, SMIC revenue at RMB 38.64 billion
15.summary: A tally of 186 A-share semiconductor companies shows combined 1H 2026 net profit of RMB 160.51 billion, up 607.2% YoY. The top three by revenue were CXMT at RMB 150.31 billion (+873.64% YoY), CECport at RMB 73.56 billion (+164.19% YoY) and SMIC at RMB 38.64 billion (+19.4% YoY). By net profit, CXMT led with RMB 77.61 billion, followed by Longsys at RMB 10.58 billion. The report did not list figures for Hua Hong or Nexchip.
15.metric: 186 companies' combined net profit RMB 160.51B (YoY +607.2%); CXMT revenue RMB 150.31B (YoY +873.64%), net profit RMB 77.61B; SMIC revenue RMB 38.64B (YoY +19.4%)
15.impact: China's chip-profit boom comes almost entirely from the memory price cycle. SMIC's revenue grew only about 20% YoY, corroborating Huawei's remark about being constrained by SMIC's 7/6nm capacity (item #4 this period) — China's foundry bottleneck is advanced-node supply, not demand. CXMT's expansion will also keep absorbing domestic equipment and engineering talent.

16.title: DeepSeek reportedly expands use of Huawei chips for model training; new supply could arrive as early as 2026Q4
16.summary: Reports say DeepSeek founder Liang Wenfeng stated that the company will expand its use of domestic chips, including Huawei's, for AI model training, saying it 'must succeed'; Huawei's next batch of chips could ship as early as 2026Q4. DeepSeek is training a 2-trillion-parameter model and planning an 8-trillion-parameter version, investing about RMB 30 billion to expand compute, and is finalizing a RMB 50 billion fundraising. The report estimates that training a model comparable to OpenAI's largest would take about 50,000 Nvidia GB300s, or about 200,000 Huawei Ascend 950s — and again cites SMIC's 7/6nm-class capacity as the limit on Huawei's AI hardware supply.
16.metric: New supply as early as 2026Q4; 2T-parameter model in training, 8T planned; compute investment ~RMB 30B; fundraising RMB 50B; ~50,000 GB300 vs ~200,000 Ascend 950
16.impact: The 50,000-vs-200,000 conversion shows domestic chips need roughly four times as many units to reach the same training scale, amplifying wafer demand at SMIC. But with 7/6nm capacity unable to grow, the bigger the demand, the wider the supply gap — SMIC's expansion and yields will be the real constraint on China's AI development in 2027.
16.conf: Unconfirmed (relayed by media, not formally announced by DeepSeek; chip counts are the report's estimates)

17.title: The 2nm smartphone processor battle begins: A20 Pro, Dimensity 9600 Pro and Snapdragon 8 Elite Gen 6 debut in the same quarter
17.summary: Apple's A20 Pro (iPhone 18 Pro series) uses TSMC 2nm and WMCM packaging, with a 20% faster CPU and 40% better GPU performance. MediaTek's Dimensity 9600 Pro uses TSMC 2nm with DTCO optimization, improving single-core performance by 17%, multi-core by 15% and peak GPU performance by 27%, and supports LPDDR6 and UFS 5. On 9/22 Qualcomm launched two 2nm flagship chips, the Snapdragon 8 Elite Gen 6 and Extreme Gen 6; the Extreme version improves CPU performance by 13%, GPU by 44% and power efficiency by 37%–40%, appearing first in phones from Xiaomi, OPPO, vivo, Honor and Motorola. Reports on Qualcomm's new chips did not disclose the foundry. In the same period, telecom carriers said iPhone 18 Pro sales in the first 3 days were up 70%.
17.metric: A20 Pro: TSMC 2nm + WMCM, CPU +20%, GPU +40%; Dimensity 9600 Pro: TSMC 2nm, single-core +17%, multi-core +15%; Snapdragon 8 Elite Extreme Gen 6: CPU +13%, GPU +44%; iPhone 18 Pro first-3-day sales +70%
17.impact: All three major smartphone SoC vendors moving to 2nm in the same quarter is direct evidence of TSMC N2 ramping in Q4 2026, consistent with this period's Commercial Times estimate of 90,000–100,000 wafers per month of 2nm capacity by year-end. WMCM also extends advanced-packaging demand from AI chips to smartphones.
17.conf: Confirmed (specs from company launches; Qualcomm's foundry not disclosed)

18.title: Samsung starts Tesla AI5 trial production early at its Taylor fab; Q2 foundry share of 5.9% is only 0.5 points ahead of SMIC
18.summary: Reports say Samsung has begun trial production and yield validation of Tesla's AI5 chip early at its fab in Taylor, Texas, ahead of the original plan for full operation in November, aiming to complete validation by end-2026 and supply in volume in 2027. The move was brought forward because its Hwaseong and Pyeongtaek fabs in Korea are fully loaded with AI chip demand. Tesla and Samsung signed a US$16.5 billion chip supply contract in 2025. In Q2 2026, Samsung's global foundry market share was 5.9% versus SMIC's 5.4%, a gap of just 0.5 percentage points. Taylor Fab 2 is slated to break ground by end-2026 and start operating around 2030 with a 1.4nm process.
18.metric: AI5 trial production ahead of the original November schedule; validation by end-2026, volume production in 2027; Tesla contract US$16.5B; Q2 foundry share Samsung 5.9% vs SMIC 5.4%; Taylor Fab 2 groundbreaking end-2026, operating ~2030 (1.4nm)
18.impact: With the market share gap to SMIC at just 0.5 points, it is clear why Samsung is rushing to bring Taylor online early. Consistent with last period's news that Samsung delayed SF1.4 to 2029 to focus on SF2, Samsung's current strategy is to lock in US 2nm capacity and anchor customers first.
18.conf: Background (originally published 2026/09/21, outside this period; early trial production is a Korean media report, not announced by Samsung)

19.title: GlobalFoundries and SMART Photonics launch the industry's first open foundry service integrating silicon and indium phosphide photonics
19.summary: Dutch indium phosphide (InP) photonic chipmaker SMART Photonics announced a partnership with GlobalFoundries to launch the industry's first open foundry service integrating silicon photonics and InP photonics. Built on GF's silicon photonics platform, it integrates SMART Photonics' lasers and semiconductor optical amplifiers using flip-chip technology. After more than a year of joint development, it is set to open fully in 2H 2027 for AI data centers, pluggable optical transceivers, lidar and more. Earlier, on 9/17, GF also announced an expanded collaboration with Marvell on next-generation optical connectivity.
19.metric: Full availability 2H 2027; integration: flip-chip; applications: AI data centers, pluggable optical modules, lidar
19.impact: What silicon photonics lacks is a light source, which makes InP laser integration key. GF fills that gap with an open-foundry model, on a timeline similar to UMC opening its 12-inch silicon photonics platform to customers in 2027 — mature-node foundries' competition in silicon photonics has entered the platform-integration stage. It also belongs to the same optical-interconnect theme as this period's Lumentum VCSEL D2D item.
19.conf: Background (originally published 2026/09/21, outside this period; company announcement)

20.title: Mature-node foundry prices head higher, squeezing consumer IC designers' gross margins
20.summary: Economic Daily News reported that rising demand for AI-related power management and control components is pushing up mature-node foundry prices. But consumer IC design houses, facing weak end-market demand, are under margin pressure because 'foundry prices are rising but chip prices can't', and low-end consumer chips are highly substitutable, with price competition from mainland Chinese peers.
